item.title: Alabama lawyer gave up career to care for parents, but court upheld cancellation of her condo deed
item.description: The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate.

item.title: DNA evidence solves 2012 murder of North Carolina student Faith Hedgepeth, 14 years later
item.description: Miguel Salguero Olivares has received a life sentence for the chilling murder of Faith Hedgepeth, whose case remained a mystery for nearly ten years. Thanks to DNA evidence, he was arrested and convicted of first-degree murder, rape, and burglary. Faith's lifeless body was found in her apartment in September 2012 after a fun night out.

item.title: After years of abandonment, 48 acres once home to Ohio's SeaWorld and Six Flags parks are set to reopen on October 25
item.description: Aurora Park at Geauga Lake will reopen to the public on October 25, focusing on outdoor recreation. This redevelopment includes seating areas, boating access, and restored structures from the amusement park era. Future phases will introduce a public beach, playground, and other recreational facilities as part of the project. The City of Aurora acquired the property in December 2024 to ensure public access.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Arctic ice had been expanding for 1,000 years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960
item.description: A recent study indicates that the Barnes Ice Cap had begun expanding nearly 2,000 years ago. This expansion was attributed to cooler summer conditions that allowed ice to grow. However, rising greenhouse gas emissions reversed this trend and caused significant ice retreat since the 1960s. Researchers emphasize that human-induced warming has disrupted natural climate patterns that favored renewed glacial growth.

item.title: Lost Joan Eardley painting found in charity shop after 64 years, selling for £29,500 for research
item.description: In an unexpected twist, a stunning landscape painting by Scottish talent Joan Eardley was discovered in an English charity shop. Named Summer Fields, the artwork fetched an impressive £29,500, with proceeds dedicated to funding medical research. After a paper label revealed its authenticity, the piece was returned to Scotland for further evaluation. This sale highlights the increasing appreciation for Eardley’s influence on mid-20th century art, celebrated in various exhibitions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: About 1,300 abuse survivors agree to an $800m NY Catholic Church settlement, pending signatures
item.description: The Catholic Archdiocese of New York has reached an $800 million settlement for around 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse. This settlement resulted from lawsuits filed under the Child Victims Act, which allowed claims despite prior time limits. Payments will be determined through an independent review process based on the severity of the abuse and its impact. The archdiocese plans to improve transparency by releasing more records related to accused clergy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Built in 1834, a 75,000-pound Métis home crossed Georgian Bay after its owner sold it for $2
item.description: The historic Labatte House, a Métis residence from 1834, is set to be carefully moved to Balm Beach to ensure its preservation. Weighing approximately 75,000 pounds, the relocation is a meticulous endeavor across Georgian Bay. This effort seeks to create a museum dedicated to Indigenous and Métis narratives in the area, with restoration scheduled to start soon and a concrete foundation expected by spring 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Crystal Drinkwalter & Jazmyn Canning built a $52K natural pond on their 65-acre land, saving $148K
item.description: On their sprawling 65-acre property, Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning took on the ambitious project of building a natural swimming pond after being deterred by high contractor fees. Through hard work, they relocated more than 100,000 pounds of rock and lined the pond by hand. It took eight water trucks to fill their 110,000-gallon pond with water. For a detailed look at this impressive feat, visit their YouTube channel.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After surviving cardiac arrest in 2023, Damar Hamlin helped 1,293 people learn CPR in one hour
item.description: Damar Hamlin set a Guinness World Record by successfully teaching hands-only CPR to 1,293 individuals at Acrisure Stadium. This event, part of a broader initiative in partnership with the American Heart Association, aimed to raise awareness about cardiac emergencies and emphasize the importance of immediate response. Fueled by his personal experience with cardiac arrest, Hamlin sought to empower his community with life-saving skills for potential emergencies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump's 250-foot arch could see construction begin November 5 despite pending legal challenge
item.description: US President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington could begin construction as early as November 5, pending final approvals. However, three military veterans and a retired architectural historian have asked a federal judge to stop the work, arguing that congressional authorisation is required. The project faces two lawsuits questioning its approval process and legality.

item.title: Israel elections: Can Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?
item.description: Israeli voters will head to the polls on October 27 in a significant election for Benjamin Netanyahu. His political future hinges on addressing security failures following the October 7 attack by Hamas. Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a primary challenger, emphasizing military accountability over Netanyahu's leadership. The election highlights divisions within the opposition and potential coalition challenges.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 24-year-old Coast Guard swimmer rescues 16 people from Pacific shipwreck after two hours in darkness
item.description: A US Coast Guard rescue swimmer undertook a challenging operation to save 16 individuals from the Pacific Ocean. The rescue followed a distress call regarding a capsized boat off Mexico's Baja California. Over 2,441 square miles were searched, but 11 victims remain missing as the search was suspended. Investigation into the vessel's circumstances is ongoing, and survivors received medical care before being processed under US immigration law.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: No need to take blood pressure pills now? Scientists are testing a device that can reduce BP by stimulating nerves
item.description: A recent study shows that stimulating the ear can help lower blood pressure. Known as transcutaneous autonomic neuromodulation, this innovative approach may offer an effective solution for managing hypertension. In a clinical trial with 63 participants who struggled with uncontrolled hypertension despite medication, those with severe cases displayed encouraging results. However, further research is essential to validate the efficacy of this non-invasive technique.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In the 1940s, Ohio built a 200-foot dam for a village; now, it’s restoring a 14-mile creek
item.description: Ohio's Cloverlick Dam, built in the 1940s, is being removed to restore the natural flow of Cloverlick Creek. This restoration project aims to improve water quality and reconnect aquatic habitats that have been disrupted for decades. Removal of the dam is expected to create a safer environment for recreational activities like fishing and kayaking. Funding for the project is being provided by the H2Ohio Rivers Program and federal grants.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Kentucky couple transferred $210,000 land for $1; appeals court upholds sale over $177,668 debt
item.description: A property transfer for just $1 has failed to shield a Kentucky couple’s land from a creditor seeking to recover an unpaid debt. In an October 23, 2026, opinion, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld an order allowing property assessed at approximately $210,000 to be sold to satisfy a judgment of $177,667.88, plus applicable costs and attorney fees.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
